selected_evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed and configured on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.0.11, listening on 10.100.0.10:53; dig confirms inventory-api.internal resolves to 10.100.0.11 and external names still resolve (forwarding works)

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
selected_evidence.summary: node2's /etc/resolv.conf set to nameserver 10.100.0.10 via nmcli; getent/dig on node2 confirm inventory-api.internal resolves to 10.100.0.11 and external domains resolve through node1

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (stream closed confirms disconnect), node1 came back with new boot_id 93e7b182 (changed from bccb87ac), revealing dnsmasq had failed to start (boot race)

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 issue diagnosed and fixed, then re-verified across another restart
selected_evidence.summary: journalctl showed 'Cannot assign requested address'; added network-online.target dependency + bind-dynamic, restarted dnsmasq (active), re-verified resolution, then rebooted node1 again: boot_id changed to 1f5a70f4, dnsmasq auto-active, inventory-api.internal and google.com resolved correctly without manual intervention
boot_id fb2aa416 and working resolution (inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.0.11) captured immediately before reboot was issued

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: node2 came back reachable after reboot; boot_id changed to 45e01511 (from fb2aa416); resolv.conf still points to 10.100.0.10 and both internal (inventory-api.internal) and external (google.com) DNS resolution confirmed working post-restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 final state healthy after both nodes restarted
selected_evidence.summary: Final check: dnsmasq active/enabled on node1, inventory-api.internal still resolves to 10.100.0.11
